title: 182. Anxiety 101: What We Do Wrong, How to Cope, and Facing Our Fears feat. Dr. David Rosmarin
description_html:
Today's guest is Dr. David Rosmarin— an associate professor at Harvard Medical School, a program director at McLean Hospital, and founder of Center for Anxiety—a practice that services over 1,000 patients per year in multiple states. Dr. Rosmarin studies the relevance of spirituality to mental health and his work has been featured in CNN, NPR, Scientific American, the Boston Globe, the Wall Street Journal, and the New York Times.

Dr. Rosmarin's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/dhrosmarin/
talk_about: The relationship between rumination & social anxiety
Ineffective (and sometimes unconscious!) ways we deal with anxiety
Ways to navigate anxiety that have helped thousands of people at his anxiety program
How to stop avoiding what’s making you anxious
Personality traits that anxious people tend to have
Supporting someone with anxiety without invalidating or enabling them
Finding professional help for your anxiety

guests: dr. david rosmarin, associate professor at harvard medical school and founder of center for anxiety
summary: dr. david rosmarin, a harvard medical school professor and founder of center for anxiety, breaks down what anxiety actually is—a misfire of our fear response that isn't dangerous or pathological. he explains how common coping mechanisms like worry, rumination, and avoidance actually amplify anxiety, and why the key to treatment is learning to lean into discomfort rather than run from it. listeners learn how exposure therapy works (when done right), how anxiety can build resilience and emotional strength when we change our relationship with it, and practical guidance on supporting someone with anxiety without enabling or invalidating them.
quote: when we learn to embrace our anxiety, it is a key to unlocking human potential.
quote_display: when we learn to EMBRACE our anxiety, it is a KEY to unlocking human POTENTIAL.
